name: Horse_ebooks
title: The Bot That Wasn't a Bot
claims: Horse_ebooks is a Twitter account and Internet phenomenon | [1]
Horse_ebooks was registered in 2010 | [1]
The account was apparently intended to promote e-books | [1]
Horse_ebooks became known for amusing non sequiturs apparently to evade spam detection | [1]
On September 24, 2013, it was revealed the account had been sold in 2011 | [1]
The sale was to promote an alternate reality game / viral marketing for an art project | [1]
The art project was by collective Synydyne and included Bear Stearns Bravo about the 2007 subprime mortgage crisis | [1]
The Twitter account has not been updated since September 24, 2013 | [1]
Creator of Horse_ebooks was believed to be Russian web developer and spammer Alexei Kouznetsov | [1]
Kouznetsov owned as many as 170 domains associated with similar efforts | [1]
Some of Kouznetsov's domains/accounts have been shut down or discontinued | [1]
Other accounts in the network included companyebooks, action_ebooks and mystery_ebooks | [1]
Horse_ebooks tweeted fragments of modified text copied from other sources | [1]
Horse_ebooks tweeted occasional promotional links to websites selling e-books associated with ClickBank | [1]
Example tweet: "I will make certain you never buy knives again," | [1]
Example tweet: "We all agree, no one looks cool," | [1]
Example tweet: "Is the dance floor calling? No," | [1]
Example tweet: "Everything happens so much" | [1]
Example tweet: "Unfortunately, as you probably already know, people" | [1]
Horse_ebooks output was described as strangely poetic and as cryptic missives read like Zen koans dropped on a keyboard | [1]
Horse_ebooks did not employ strategies of mass-following and unsolicited replies | [1]
Because it didn't use typical spammer techniques, the account was not closed as Twitter spam accounts frequently are | [1]
Before September 2013, it had more than 200,000 followers | [1]
On September 24, 2013, it was announced Horse_ebooks was part of a multi-year performance art piece by BuzzFeed employee Jacob Bakkila | [1]
Bakkila approached Kuznetsov in 2011 to buy the account, Kuznetsov agreed | [1]
Since 2011, Horse_ebooks had been operated by Bakkila | [1]
Followers noticed a change on September 14, 2011 when tweets began posting "via web" instead of "via Horse ebooks" | [1]
After September 14, 2011, ClickBank tweets dropped and "funny" tweets increased | [1]
Followers speculated the spam algorithm changed or a hacker took over the account password | [1]
On the day of the reveal, Bakkila and others performed at an art installation where fans could call in and have tweets read | [1]
After the announcement, Bakkila stopped tweeting on the account | [1]
Horse_ebooks inspired fan art, fan fiction, unofficial merchandise, T-shirts, and Horse_eComics | [1]
Horse_eComics was a Tumblr blog by artist Burton Durand | [1]
UGO Networks named Horse_ebooks one of the best Twitter feeds in 2011 | [1]
Time.com named Horse_ebooks one of the best Twitter feeds in 2012 | [1]
John Herrman at Splitsider wrote Horse_ebooks might be the best Twitter account that has ever existed | [1]
Memphis Barker at The Independent described Twitter as 'devastated' by the human-run revelation | [1]
The Atlantic named Horse_ebooks "the most successful piece of cyber fiction" | [1]
Synydyne is an artist collective formed in 2006 responsible for performance art and alternate reality game projects | [1]
Synydyne is led by internet artists Thomas Bender and Jacob Bakkila | [1]
Synydyne's projects include Horse_ebooks, Bear Stearns Bravo, Pronunciation Book, and This is My Milwaukee | [1]
Bakkila explained in a 2015 interview that Synydyne projects are designed to spread quickly or be difficult to access | [1]
Burton Durand was a 28-year-old art director at a design firm in Lafayette, La. | [2]
Durand started drawing comics inspired by horse_ebooks messages in December | [2]
Another artist posted a pencil drawing inspired by "leg butt" and Durand decided to make more | [2]
Durand's Tumblr blog attracted about 600 followers | [2]
Durand sold original cartoons online for $30 apiece | [2]
Durand admitted there is a small niche demographic for his creations | [2]

sources.title: Web Comic Draws Inspiration From a Twitter Spammer - The New York Times
